title: 4 Space Mysteries Nobody Can Solve
next: Tomorrow: the history of the universe in one year!
description:
A signal from space that lasted 72 seconds. A cigar-shaped rock from another star. A star that dims for no clear reason. And what's inside a black hole? The Cosmozibs crew investigates 4 space mysteries that real scientists still can't solve!

{{chapters}}

A new episode every day. Join the crew: https://www.youtube.com/@Cosmozibs?sub_confirmation=1

Voices in this video are AI-generated. Every fact is checked with the sources below.

#space #spacefacts #spacemysteries

lines.say: Hey, space cadets! Today we're going on a mystery hunt!
A strange signal from deep space. A weird rock from another star.
A star that dims for no clear reason. And the darkest mystery of all: what's inside a black hole?
Mysteries? The only mystery I care about is who ate my space cookies.
Here's the plan. Four mysteries, four clues, and a quiz after each one.
I'm the best detective in the galaxy! Probably!
Real scientists still can't solve these. Maybe one day you will! Tick tock, let's go!

short.title: The Space Signal Nobody Can Explain

lines.say: In the summer of nineteen seventy seven, a giant radio telescope heard something from deep space.
A super strong signal. It lasted for seventy two seconds. Then it was gone.
Wait... WHAT? A message from space?! How could this happen?!
A scientist named Jerry Ehman found it on a computer printout. He circled it in red pen and wrote one word next to it.
Wow! That's why everyone calls it the Wow signal!
It seemed to come from the direction of the Sagittarius stars. Scientists listened there again and again, but they never heard it a second time.
Typical. Somebody calls once, and then never calls back.
Bonus fact! The telescope was called Big Ear. It wasn't a dish. It was a huge, flat metal field!
So was it aliens? Please say it was aliens!
Nobody knows! Some scientists think a cloud of gas in space suddenly glowed very bright, for a moment.
Others think it was something we just don't understand yet. That's why it's still a mystery!
Hello, space! If that was you, please call again!
Quiz time! How long did the Wow signal last? Seven seconds, seventy two seconds, or seven hours?

show.q: How long did the Wow! signal last?

lines.say: Seventy two seconds! Just over one minute, and then silence.
Next mystery: a visitor from another star!

short.title: A Rock From Another Star Visited Us

lines.say: In twenty seventeen, a telescope in Hawaii spotted something zooming past the Sun.
It wasn't from our solar system at all. It came from another star! The first visitor like that we had ever confirmed.
Wait... WHAT? A rock from another star?! How could this happen?!
Scientists named it Oumuamua. In Hawaiian, that means a messenger from afar arriving first.
And it was a weird shape. Long and thin, like a cigar. About ten times longer than it was wide!
It was racing at about three hundred thousand kilometers per hour, close to the Sun!
Hey, it's a rock like me. Finally, someone famous in my family!
But here's the strange part. As it left, it sped up a tiny bit. Like a comet, which pushes out gas. But nobody saw a comet tail!
A rock with a secret engine? Was it a spaceship?!
Most scientists think it was just a natural rock or a piece of ice. But it left too fast for us to check up close.
Bonus fact! It wasn't the last visitor. In twenty twenty five, astronomers spotted a third one, called three I ATLAS!
More rocks? This is the best day of my life.
Quiz time! What shape was Oumuamua? Round like a ball, long like a cigar, or flat like a pancake?
Long like a cigar! About ten times longer than it was wide.
Next mystery: a star that keeps fading!

short.title: The Star That Dims for No Clear Reason

lines.say: Far away, there's a star that does something really odd. Sometimes it gets much darker!
The Kepler space telescope watched it for years. Some days, its light dropped by up to twenty two percent!
Wait... WHAT? Who turned down the lights?! How could this happen?!
When a planet passes in front of a star, the star dims a tiny bit. But a planet blocks maybe one percent. Not twenty two!
And the dips came at random times. No pattern at all!
Scientists call it Tabby's star, after Tabetha Boyajian, the astronomer who led the team that studied it.
A star that keeps hiding? Smart. I hide from homework too.
Bonus fact! The first people to spot those weird dips weren't professors. They were volunteers, checking telescope data from home!
Some people even said: maybe aliens built something giant around it!
Fun idea! But later telescopes found clues. The dimming was stronger in some colors of light than others.
That points to clouds of tiny dust grains drifting in front of the star. But where all that dust comes from is still a mystery!
So it's not aliens. It's space dust. I'm a little sad, but also a little amazed.
Quiz time! How much did Tabby's star dim? One percent, twenty two percent, or one hundred percent?

show.q: How much did Tabby's star dim?

lines.say: Up to twenty two percent! Way too much for a planet.
And now, the biggest mystery of all.
What is inside a black hole? The answer is... nobody knows!
A black hole has so much gravity that nothing can escape. Not even light!
Wait... WHAT? Not even light?! How could this happen?!
Around it is a border called the event horizon. It's not a surface you can stand on. It's more like a point of no return.
Anything that crosses it can never come back out. So we can't look inside, and no signal can tell us what's in there.
If something got too close, gravity would stretch it long and thin. Scientists really call this spaghettification!
Spaghetti? Now I'm hungry. Thanks a lot, universe.
Bonus fact! In the middle of our own galaxy sits a giant black hole called Sagittarius A star.
It has about four million times the mass of our Sun. But don't worry, it's very, very far away from Earth.
Phew! Nobody is getting spaghettified today!
Scientists have even taken pictures of the glowing ring of gas around black holes. The middle stays dark.
What happens to matter deep inside? Our best science can't explain it yet. Maybe a future space cadet will crack it!
Quiz time! What can escape from a black hole? Light, rockets, or nothing at all?

show.q: What can escape a black hole?

lines.say: Nothing! Once something crosses the event horizon, it can't come back. Not even light.
Wow. Okay, detectives, time to speed things up!
Speed round! Five quick facts. Ready? Go!
One! The Wow signal was never heard again, even after many searches.
Two! Oumuamua was about four hundred meters long. That's as long as four soccer fields!
Three! Tabby's star was found in data from the Kepler space telescope.
Four! Black holes are invisible, but we can spot them by the glowing gas and stars around them.
Five! Light from the Sun reaches Earth in about eight minutes. A black hole would never let it go!
Whoa. My detective brain is full!
That's four space mysteries! Which one do you want scientists to solve first?
Think about it! The Wow signal, the cigar rock, the fading star, or the black hole?
The cigar rock. Obviously. It's family.
Here's a challenge. Tell a friend your best guess for one mystery. Real scientists start with a guess too!

Subscribe and join the crew. See you tomorrow, space cadets!
